sources.inspection_note: Read original v2 pp.2–5: §3 Eq.7 and Fig.1 define the min of unclipped/clipped surrogate and asymmetric plateaus, not a hard ratio bound; §5 Eq.9 supplies value squared error and Algorithm1 collects with old policy then reuses samples for K epochs. A finite one-step reduction does not establish token-level language-model quality.

Read original v3 §3 pp.3–4: SFT fine-tunes a pretrained LM; Eq.1–2 give Bradley–Terry reward comparison; Eq.3 uses KL(policy||fixed reference), with the reference initialized to the initial SFT model. This toy adds analytical exact finite KL and uses reward-only critic targets; it is not asserted to match every LLM PPO recipe.
Read torch.optim.SGD signature, update pseudocode, step and defaults momentum=0, weight_decay=0, maximize=False. With a gradient and these defaults, theta is updated by theta-lr*gradient.
Read CrossEntropyLoss input logits/target definitions and label_smoothing: mix original ground truth with the uniform class distribution. This target is not a guarantee about learned probabilities.
Read Categorical constructor, normalized logits, integer sample support0..K-1 and log_prob; leading axes are batch axes and the last is the action axis.
Read no_grad reverse-mode recording semantics including factory-function and forward-AD exceptions; this lesson does not invoke those exceptions.

Read Module.requires_grad_: sets module parameter requires_grad flags in place. It does not itself erase existing gradients; these lesson modules are freshly created or deepcopied before any backward.
Read Optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True): resets optimized gradients, with None causing a parameter to be skipped. The lesson description of clearing prior gradients is accurate.

Retrieved the immutable original project report at commit1df335318bda03fd771807f66976953231d5a00b; retrievalSHA95c8ee6c89b009a9646903c1bccaa6a0ace53786a608307d50ba7d9fb0a09172 exactly equals local record bytes. Every row/candidate/feature/label, greedy success and first-rollout observation was independently inspected and recomputed. It supports one fixed historical CPU run, not portable timing.
Read gather index/output shape and axis semantics: [1,4] scores gathered by [1,1] indices produce [1,1]; input/index do not broadcast.
Read squeeze(dim): removes only specified size-one axes; squeeze(1) retains the batch axis and yields[1].
Read Tensor.backward: chain-rule gradients accumulate in graph leaves; the scalar loss needs no explicit upstream gradient.
Read functional.cross_entropy signature/label_smoothing: the same ground-truth/uniform mixture; this is the actual function called by the toy.
Read Linear weight/bias shapes and uniform initialization. New layers have random parameters; the complete toy constructs its new policy without a pretrained weight load.
